scene information in a texture that can be used by post effects. To use a map renderer (a concrete subclass of this generic class): Add the component to a GameObject in your scene. Configure the properties. To render your own type of map: Create a shader that can render the information you need. (Optional) Create a background shader to render the background of the map. Create a new class inheriting from MapProperties, that sets up the material properties for your shader (and background shader if needed). Create extend from MapRenderer<TMapProperties> class using your new MapProperties type as the generic parameter. Generally the class can be empty (a concrete type is needed to show up in the inspector). If your camera properties change (through animation or scripting) you need to set Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.Mapping.MapRenderer<TMapProperties>.updateCameraEachFrame to true. You may need to set the execution order to make sure this script executes after the code that updates the camera. If your source camera itself changes, you set SourceCamera. Properties LayerMask Gets and sets the layer mask used to select which objects are rendered into the map. public LayerMask LayerMask { get; set; } Property Value LayerMask MapProperties Gets the map properties for this map renderer. public TMapProperties MapProperties { get; } Property Value TMapProperties SourceCamera Gets and sets the source camera used to render the map. public Camera SourceCamera { get; set; } Property Value Camera UpdateCameraEachFrame Gets and sets whether to update the camera properties each frame. public bool UpdateCameraEachFrame { get; set; } Property Value bool UpdateRenderListEachFrame Gets and sets whether to update the list of renderers each frame in playmode. public bool UpdateRenderListEachFrame { get; set; } Property Value bool UpdateRenderListEachFrameInEditor Gets and sets whether to update the list of renderers each frame in edit mode. This only has an effect when not playing. public bool UpdateRenderListEachFrameInEditor { get; set; } Property Value bool Methods RefreshRendererList() Updates the list of renderers to be drawn. public void RefreshRendererList() Remarks This can potentially be slow, so be careful calling it each frame.

api/Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing..summary: Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects Classes AddTexturePostProcess A post process that overlays a texture on top of the scene, respecting transparency. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#add-texture. AdjustGammaPostProcess A post process that adjusts the gamma of the image. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#adjust-gamma. AdjustSaturationPostProcess A post process that adjusts the saturation of the image. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#adjust-saturation. BilateralFilterPostProcess A post process that smooths the image using an edge-preserving, noise-reducing filter. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#bilateral-filter. BlendTexturePostProcess A post process that blends a texture over the scene at a configurable opacity. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#blend-texture. BoxBlurPostProcess A post process that applies a uniform blur by averaging neighbor pixels colors. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#box-blur. ConvexHullMapPostProcess A post process that gradually shifts colors toward the provided primaries, producing posterized, clustered, or palette–constrained looks. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#convex-hull-map. DesaturatePostProcess A post process that converts the image to grayscale using luminosity. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#desaturate. GaussianBlurPostProcess A post process that applies a smooth, natural-looking blur using a Gaussian weight curve. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#gaussian-blur. InvertPostProcess Inverts the colors of the image. MaxPostProcess A post process that replaces each pixel with the maximum color value found in its neighborhood. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#max-filter. MinPostProcess A post process that replaces each pixel with the minimum color value found in its neighborhood. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#min-filter. MixboxConvexHullMapPostProcess A post process that pushes each pixel’s color toward chosen primaries using convex-hull projection, but blends them with Mixbox for more natural, smoother color transitions than normal interpolation. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#mixbox-convex-hull-map. PixelatePostProcess A post process that applies a pixelation effect to the image by sampling blocks of pixels instead of individual texels. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#pixelate. PowerMeanPostProcess A post process that blurs the image by computing a power mean (p-norm mean) of neighboring pixels. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#power-mean. QuadToneMapPostProcess A smooth 4-way threshold shader using inverse lerp (linear blend). Interpolates between Low–Mid0, Mid0–Mid1, and Mid1–High based on lightness. Values below LowValue use LowColor, above HighValue use HighColor. QuantizePostProcess A post process that reduces the number of distinct color values in the image, creating a posterized or stylized effect. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#quantize. SimpleOutlinePostProcess A post process that produces an outline. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#simple-outline. TriToneMapPostProcess Maps the image’s tones to three colors (low, mid, and high) based on lightness, smoothly blending between them using inverse linear interpolation. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#tri-tone-map.

api/Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing..summary: Interface IPostProcess Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing Assembly Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.dll ⭐ Interface for post process effects. public interface IPostProcess Remarks Intended for the built-in render pipeline. Any class that implements this interface can be used as a post process with PostProcessRunner. Usually PostProcess is a suitable base class for custom post effects, but in cases you want to have the implementation complete, you can use this interface. Properties enabled Whether the post process is enabled. bool enabled { get; } Property Value bool Remarks The PostProcessRunner ignores it if disabled. Methods OnRenderImage(RenderTexture, RenderTexture) The function that performs the post process effect. void OnRenderImage(RenderTexture sourceTexture, RenderTexture destTexture) Parameters sourceTexture RenderTexture The full screen source texture. destTexture RenderTexture The render target for the post process. Remarks A typical implementation uses UnityEngine.Graphics.Blit(UnityEngine.Texture, UnityEngine.RenderTexture, UnityEngine.Material) to perform the post-process effect.

pipeline. This script should be placed on a Camera. It calls OnRenderImage(RenderTexture, RenderTexture) on all children with components that implement IPostProcess of the postProcessRoot configured in this inspector. This allows you to have post-processes in separate objects and make it easier to manage if you are experimenting with many processes at the same time. So to add a post process to your camera: Add this script to the camera. Add an empty GameObject in your scene and call it PostEffects (or similar). Add a child object for each post process you want to add (e.g. AdjustGammaPostProcess), and add the post process script to it. Any script that implements IPostProcess will work. This class can also be used to group a stack of effects as a single IPostProcess, so it can be used by effects that require an IPostProcess. In this case, you need not add the script to a camera (an empty game object will do fine). In this case, the OnRenderImage method will be called by the effect that requires this IPostProcess. pipeline. This script should be placed on a Camera. It calls OnRenderImage(RenderTexture, RenderTexture) on all children with components that implement IPostProcess of the postProcessRoot configured in this inspector. This allows you to have post-processes in separate objects and make it easier to manage if you are experimenting with many processes at the same time. So to add a post process to your camera: Add this script to the camera. Add an empty GameObject in your scene and call it PostEffects (or similar). Add a child object for each post process you want to add (e.g. AdjustGammaPostProcess), and add the post process script to it. Any script that implements IPostProcess will work. This class can also be used to group a stack of effects as a single IPostProcess, so it can be used by effects that require an IPostProcess. In this case, you need not add the script to a camera (an empty game object will do fine). In this case, the OnRenderImage method will be called by the effect that requires this IPostProcess. api/Gamelogic.Fx.CrossHatching.Orientati.title: Enum OrientationScheme | Gamelogic Fx
api/Gamelogic.Fx.CrossHatching.Orientati.summary: Enum OrientationScheme Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.CrossHatching Assembly Gamelogic.Fx.CrossHatching.dll Schemes for orienting hatch layers. public enum OrientationScheme Fields Fixed = 0 Relative to the first layer, layers are rotated by a fixed angle. That is: Layer 0: 0 degrees Layer 1: 90 degrees Layer 2: 45 degrees Layer 3: 135 degrees Layer 4: 22.5 degrees Layer 5: 112.5 degrees Layer 6: 67.5 degrees Layer 7: 157.5 degrees After this the pattern repeats. Golden = 2 The angles are multiples of 180 times the golden ratio (approximately 1.61803398875). This is the best compromise between maximizing the angle difference between any present layers, and being the same regardless of the number of layers. No two layers will ever overlap exactly. Parallel = 3 The layers are all aligned. Uniform = 1 The angles are uniformly distributed between 0 and 180 degrees according to the number of layers. For example for 3 layers, the angles would be: Layer 0: 0 degrees Layer 1: 60 degrees Layer 2: 120 degrees

api/Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.FundamentalRe.summary: Class FundamentalRegion Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering Assembly Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.dll A dither bias matrix whose valid entries are shaped by a parallelogram in a lattice. [Serializable] public sealed class FundamentalRegion : ISerializationCallbackReceiver Inheritance object FundamentalRegion Implements ISerializationCallbackReceiver Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The fundamental region is the parallelogram spanned by basis vectors A = (x0, 0) and B = (x1, y1). It contains Count = x0 * y1 lattice points, each with a bias value stored in Matrix. The matrix is sized to the axis-aligned bounding rect of those Count points; positions inside the bounding rect but outside the parallelogram are filled with -1. Call RecomputeBoundsAndReshape() after changing X0 or Point1 to resize the matrix and recompute the lookup dictionary. RebuildDictionaryIfNeeded() is called automatically before any read that requires the dictionary. Properties Count The number of points in the fundamental region. Equal to x0 * y1. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Matrix Gets the bias matrix. Its size equals the bounding rect of the fundamental region. public FloatMatrix Matrix { get; } Property Value FloatMatrix NormalizedValues Returns a copy of Values with all elements normalized to [0, 1]. If all values are equal the array is filled with zeros. The array is allocated once per size; callers should not retain a reference across frames. public float[] NormalizedValues { get; } Property Value float[] Offset The bounding rect origin of the fundamental region in grid space. Matrix position (mx, my) corresponds to grid point (mx + Offset.x, my + Offset.y). public Vector2Int Offset { get; } Property Value Vector2Int Point1 Gets or sets basis vector B = (x1, y1). The y-component must be positive. public Vector2Int Point1 { get; set; } Property Value Vector2Int Values Returns an array of Count bias values in fundamental-region index order (i.e. Values[i] is the bias for the i-th lattice point as enumerated by IndexToGridPoint(int, int, int, int)). The array is allocated once per size and filled on every call, so callers should not retain a reference across frames. public float[] Values { get; } Property Value float[] X0 Gets or sets the x-component of basis vector A = (x0, 0). Must be positive. public int X0 { get; set; } Property Value int Methods GetIndex(Vector2Int) Returns the fundamental region index (0..Count-1) for a grid point, or -1 if not in the region. public int GetIndex(Vector2Int gridPoint) Parameters gridPoint Vector2Int Returns int IsInFundamentalRegion(Vector2Int) Returns true if the given grid point is one of the Count fundamental region points. public bool IsInFundamentalRegion(Vector2Int gridPoint) Parameters gridPoint Vector2Int Returns bool RebuildDictionaryIfNeeded() Restores the lookup dictionary if it is null (e.g. after domain reload). If the serialized matrix dimensions are already correct, only the dictionary is rebuilt. If dimensions are inconsistent, falls back to a full reshape. public void RebuildDictionaryIfNeeded() RecomputeBoundsAndReshape() Recomputes the bounding box from the current params and reshapes the matrix to fit, preserving bias values at grid points that survive the resize. New region cells are set to 0; non-region cells to -1. Also rebuilds the lookup dictionary. Called automatically by the X0 and Point1 setters. public void RecomputeBoundsAndReshape() Reset() Sets all fundamental region cells to 0 and all out-of-region cells to -1. public void Reset() SetFrom(FundamentalRegion) Copies parameters and matrix values from other. The lookup dictionary is copied directly without a full rebuild. public void SetFrom(FundamentalRegion other) Parameters other FundamentalRegion

Returns Vector2Int Remarks The fundamental region is the parallelogram with basis vectors A = (x0, 0) and B = (x1, y1). It contains Count = |x0 * y1| lattice points with indices 0 .. Count-1. [Serializable] public class GridBiasDitherProperties : ShaderProperties Inheritance object ShaderProperties GridBiasDitherProperties Inherited Members ShaderProperties.MaterialVersion ShaderProperties.IncMaterialVersion() ShaderProperties.Shader ShaderProperties.RequiresDepthTexture ShaderProperties.RequiresNormalsTexture ShaderProperties.OnValidate() ShaderProperties.OnEnable() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties DitherAmountMax Gets or sets the maximum dither bias, in the range [-1, 1]. public float DitherAmountMax { get; set; } Property Value float DitherAmountMin Gets or sets the minimum dither bias, in the range [-1, 1]. public float DitherAmountMin { get; set; } Property Value float FundamentalRegionRGB Gets the dither fundamental region for all three color channels. public FundamentalRegionRGB FundamentalRegionRGB { get; } Property Value FundamentalRegionRGB GridType Gets or sets the cell geometry used for the dither grid. public GridType GridType { get; set; } Property Value GridType LevelCount Gets or sets the number of quantization levels per color channel. public int3 LevelCount { get; set; } Property Value int3 PixelSize Gets or sets the size of the dither pattern in pixels. public Vector2 PixelSize { get; set; } Property Value Vector2 ShaderName Gets the name of the shader used by this property set. public override string ShaderName { get; } Property Value string Remarks This name is passed to the internal shader lookup system when the properties are enabled. It should match the full shader path as defined in the shader file. Smoothness Gets or sets the smoothness of the dither transition, in the range [0, 1]. public float Smoothness { get; set; } Property Value float Methods CheckMaterialVersion() Checks whether any condition requires the owning material to be recreated, and calls IncMaterialVersion() if so. public override void CheckMaterialVersion() Remarks The owning post-process calls this method at the top of each render, before fetching the effect material. This guarantees that staleness detection and material recreation happen in the same frame, with no visible lag. Override this in subclasses whose properties can change size independently of normal inspector validation — for example, float arrays, texture arrays, or compute buffers whose element count is driven by user-editable data. Compare the current state against a stored "last seen" snapshot and call IncMaterialVersion() on a mismatch. See Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.PostProcessing.Effects.DitherMatrixBiasProperties for a worked example: it tracks each channel matrix's FloatMatrix.SizeVersion and increments the material version whenever any matrix is resized. SetMaterialProperties(Material) Applies all shader-related properties to the given material. public override void SetMaterialProperties(Material effectMaterial) Parameters effectMaterial Material Remarks Subclasses should override this method and set all relevant shader uniforms (for example, floats, vectors, colors, textures, and keywords). Do not call IncMaterialVersion() here. By the time this method is called the material has already been fetched, so any increment would take effect one frame late. Staleness checks belong in CheckMaterialVersion().

api/Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.PostProcessin.summary: Enum ToolMode Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.PostProcessing.Effects Assembly Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.dll Controls which visualization the grid bias dither effect renders. public enum ToolMode Fields Bias = 1 Raw bias values from the fundamental region matrix. Index = 2 Grid colorIndex encoded across two channels: R = column (offsetX), G = row (offsetY), both normalized to [0, 1]. Each fundamental-region cell gets a unique (R, G) colour. Normal = 0 Normal dithered output.

FundamentalRegion A dither bias matrix whose valid entries are shaped by a parallelogram in a lattice. FundamentalRegionRGB Three FundamentalRegion instances — one per color channel — plus a shared "all-channels" region, with a Locked flag that determines which regions are active. GridTypeFieldAttribute Applied to a FundamentalRegion or FundamentalRegionRGB field to enable grid-type-aware editor UI: row indentation (half-cell stagger per row) and Z± shift buttons when the active grid type is Hex. HexFundamentalRegionPresets Contains preset fundamental regions for the hex dither bias system. HexUtils Utility functions for hex grid coordinate conversions. RectFundamentalRegionPresets Contains preset fundamental regions for the rect dither bias system.

[Serializable] public abstract class MapProperties : ShaderProperties Inheritance object ShaderProperties MapProperties Derived DepthMapProperties IDMapProperties NormalMapProperties UVMapProperties Inherited Members ShaderProperties.ShaderName ShaderProperties.MaterialVersion ShaderProperties.IncMaterialVersion() ShaderProperties.Shader ShaderProperties.RequiresDepthTexture ShaderProperties.RequiresNormalsTexture ShaderProperties.Requirements ShaderProperties.GetActiveShaderFeatureKeywords() ShaderProperties.SetMaterialProperties(Material) ShaderProperties.CheckMaterialVersion() ShaderProperties.OnValidate() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A map encodes per-object or per-pixel information (such as IDs, UVs, depth-related data, or custom attributes) into a render texture that can later be consumed by post-processing effects. MapProperties acts as the configuration layer between map-rendering infrastructure (such as ObjectInfoRenderer in the built-in pipeline or GLMapRendererFeature in URP) and the shaders used to generate the map. Implementations typically: Specify the main map shader via MapProperties.ShaderName. Optionally specify a background shader via BackgroundShaderName. Expose serialized fields that control how objects write data into the map. Apply per-material and per-renderer state in the appropriate override methods. Properties BackgroundColor The color used to clear the render texture before any rendering takes place. public virtual Color BackgroundColor { get; } Property Value Color BackgroundShader Gets the resolved background shader. public Shader BackgroundShader { get; } Property Value Shader The background Shader, or null if no background pass is used. BackgroundShaderName The name of the shader used to render the background when rendering this object info. protected virtual string BackgroundShaderName { get; } Property Value string Remarks It is OK for this to return null if no background shader is needed, in which the BackgroundColor will appear. This property should always return the same value during the lifetime of this MapProperties. Methods OnEnable() Called when the map properties are enabled. public override void OnEnable() Remarks The default implementation resolves both the main map shader (via OnEnable()) and the optional background shader. Subclasses overriding this method should normally call base.OnEnable(). SetBackgroundMaterialProperties(Material) Applies background-specific properties to the background material. public virtual void SetBackgroundMaterialProperties(Material material) Parameters material Material The material created from BackgroundShader. Remarks Override this method to configure background shader uniforms such as clear color, gradients, or other map-wide background parameters. SetRendererProperties(MaterialPropertyBlock, Renderer) Applies per-renderer properties before drawing a renderer into the map. public virtual void SetRendererProperties(MaterialPropertyBlock block, Renderer renderer) Parameters block MaterialPropertyBlock The MaterialPropertyBlock used for this draw call. renderer Renderer The renderer currently being drawn into the map. Remarks Override this method to set renderer-specific data such as object IDs, per-object colors, UV transforms, or custom attributes.

api/Gamelogic.Fx.PostProcessing.ShaderPr.summary: Class ShaderProperties Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.PostProcessing Assembly Gamelogic.Fx.dll Defines a serializable set of properties used to configure a specific post-processing shader. [Serializable] public abstract class ShaderProperties Inheritance object ShaderProperties Derived ConvexHullHatchProperties MixboxConvexHullHatchProperties SimpleHatchProperties DitherGridBiasProperties DitherMatrixBiasProperties DitherTextureBiasProperties MapProperties AddTextureProperties AdjustGammaProperties AdjustSaturationProperties BlendTextureProperties ConvexHullMapProperties DesaturateProperties InvertProperties MixboxConvexHullMapProperties PixelateProperties QuadToneMapProperties QuantizeProperties SimpleOutlineProperties TriToneMapProperties SeparableShaderProperties Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A ShaderProperties instance acts as the bridge between inspector-exposed settings and the underlying shader uniforms. When enabled, this class attempts to load the shader specified by ShaderName and stores a reference to it so the shader is included correctly in builds. Subclasses typically: Provide the shader name via ShaderName. Expose serialized fields that represent shader parameters. Override SetMaterialProperties(Material) to apply those parameters. Override CheckMaterialVersion() if any property change requires material recreation. Properties MaterialVersion A generation counter that increments whenever the owning material must be destroyed and recreated. public int MaterialVersion { get; } Property Value int Remarks Consumers (such as Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.PostProcess<TShaderProperties> and the Dither Designer preview renderer) each maintain their own "last seen" copy of this value. When their copy differs from MaterialVersion, they destroy their cached material and create a new one before the next render. Do not increment this directly; call IncMaterialVersion() instead. See the block comment on the ShaderProperties source file for a full description of the material version system. Requirements Names of optional external packages this property set's shader depends on for one of its shader_feature keywords (for example "Mixbox"). public virtual IEnumerable<string> Requirements { get; } Property Value IEnumerable<string> Remarks Used by the editor-time shader variant collector (see EffectShaderVariantCollectionUtils) to know which package-presence keywords (such as GAMELOGIC_HAS_MIXBOX) to record for this shader, alongside the keywords from GetActiveShaderFeatureKeywords(). Unlike RequiresDepthTexture and RequiresNormalsTexture - a small, fixed set read by one runtime consumer - this covers an open-ended, growing set of optional third-party dependencies, so new ones are added by overriding this in the relevant subclass rather than by widening this base class further. Empty by default. Override to return the relevant requirement name(s) if this shader declares a shader_feature keyword gated on a package that might not be installed. RequiresDepthTexture Indicates whether this shader requires access to the camera depth texture. public virtual bool RequiresDepthTexture { get; } Property Value bool Remarks Override and return true if the shader samples depth information. This is used by higher-level systems to enable the correct camera flags. RequiresNormalsTexture Indicates whether this shader requires access to the camera normals texture. public virtual bool RequiresNormalsTexture { get; } Property Value bool Remarks Override and return true if the shader samples scene normals. This is used by higher-level systems to ensure normals are generated when needed. Shader Gets the resolved shader instance. public Shader Shader { get; } Property Value Shader The loaded Shader, or null if it could not be found. ShaderName Gets the name of the shader used by this property set. public abstract string ShaderName { get; } Property Value string Remarks This name is passed to the internal shader lookup system when the properties are enabled. It should match the full shader path as defined in the shader file. Methods CheckMaterialVersion() Checks whether any condition requires the owning material to be recreated, and calls IncMaterialVersion() if so. public virtual void CheckMaterialVersion() Remarks The owning post-process calls this method at the top of each render, before fetching the effect material. This guarantees that staleness detection and material recreation happen in the same frame, with no visible lag. Override this in subclasses whose properties can change size independently of normal inspector validation — for example, float arrays, texture arrays, or compute buffers whose element count is driven by user-editable data. Compare the current state against a stored "last seen" snapshot and call IncMaterialVersion() on a mismatch. See Gamelogic.Fx.Dithering.PostProcessing.Effects.DitherMatrixBiasProperties for a worked example: it tracks each channel matrix's FloatMatrix.SizeVersion and increments the material version whenever any matrix is resized. GetActiveShaderFeatureKeywords() Gets the shader_feature keywords that are currently active (enabled) on this property set, given its current serialized values. public IEnumerable<string> GetActiveShaderFeatureKeywords() Returns IEnumerable<string> Remarks Used by the editor-time shader variant collector (see EffectShaderVariantCollectionUtils) to work out which keyword combinations are actually configured across the project, since materials for these effects are created at runtime and never exist as serialized assets that Unity's normal shader-feature usage stripping can see. Discovered by reflection over fields whose type implements IShaderFeatureKeyword (such as BoolKeyword and EnumKeyword<TEnum>) - subclasses don't need to override this. Compiled out of Player builds; always empty outside the editor. Pipeline keywords (GAMELOGIC_HAS_URP, GAMELOGIC_HAS_URP_RENDER_GRAPH) are not listed here - they apply to every shader unconditionally and are supplied separately by PipelineDefiner.GetActivePipelineKeywords. IncMaterialVersion() Increments MaterialVersion, signalling all consumers that their cached material is stale and must be recreated before the next render. public void IncMaterialVersion() Remarks Call this from CheckMaterialVersion() when a staleness condition is detected. Do not call it from SetMaterialProperties(Material) — by the time that method runs, the material has already been fetched, so incrementing there would defer recreation to the next frame. OnEnable() Called when the owning component or asset is enabled. public virtual void OnEnable() Remarks The default implementation resolves the shader using ShaderName. Subclasses overriding this method should normally call base.OnEnable(). OnValidate() Called when serialized values are changed in the inspector. public virtual void OnValidate() Remarks Override this method to clamp values, enforce invariants, or perform lightweight validation in response to inspector edits. SetMaterialProperties(Material) Applies all shader-related properties to the given material. public virtual void SetMaterialProperties(Material material) Parameters material Material The material created for the post process effect, using the shader defined by ShaderName. Remarks Subclasses should override this method and set all relevant shader uniforms (for example, floats, vectors, colors, textures, and keywords). Do not call IncMaterialVersion() here. By the time this method is called the material has already been fetched, so any increment would take effect one frame late. Staleness checks belong in CheckMaterialVersion().

api/Gamelogic.Fx.URP.PostProcessing.Effe.title: Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.URP.PostProcessing.Effects | Gamelogic Fx
api/Gamelogic.Fx.URP.PostProcessing.Effe.summary: Namespace Gamelogic.Fx.URP.PostProcessing.Effects Classes GLAddTextureRendererFeature A post process that overlays a texture on top of the scene, respecting transparency. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#add-texture. GLAdjustGammaRendererFeature A post process that adjusts the gamma of the image. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#adjust-gamma. GLAdjustSaturationRendererFeature A post process that adjusts the saturation of the image. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#adjust-saturation. GLBilateralFilterRendererFeature A post process that smooths the image using an edge-preserving, noise-reducing filter. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#bilateral-filter. GLBlendTextureRendererFeature A post process that blends a texture over the scene at a configurable opacity. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#blend-texture. GLBoxBlurRendererFeature A post process that applies a uniform blur by averaging neighbour pixels colors. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#box-blur. GLConvexHullMapRendererFeature A post process that gradually shifts colors toward the provided primaries, producing posterized, clustered, or palette–constrained looks. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#convex-hull-map. GLDesaturateRendererFeature A post process that converts the image to grayscale using luminosity. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#desaturate. GLGaussianBlurRendererFeature A post process that applies a smooth, natural-looking blur using a Gaussian weight curve. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#gaussian-blur. GLInvertRendererFeature Inverts the colors of the image. GLMaxRendererFeature A post process that replaces each pixel with the maximum color value found in its neighborhood. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#max-filter. GLMinRendererFeature A post process that replaces each pixel with the minimum color value found in its neighborhood. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#min-filter. GLMixboxConvexHullMapRendererFeature A post process that pushes each pixel’s color toward chosen primaries using convex-hull projection, but blends them with Mixbox for more natural, smoother color transitions than normal interpolation. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#mixbox-convex-hull-map. GLPixelateRendererFeature A post process that applies a pixelation effect to the image by sampling blocks of pixels instead of individual texels. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#pixelate. GLPowerMeanRendererFeature A post process that blurs the image by computing a power mean (p-norm mean) of neighboring pixels. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#power-mean. GLQuadToneMapRendererFeature A smooth 4-way threshold shader using inverse lerp (linear blend). Interpolates between Low–Mid0, Mid0–Mid1, and Mid1–High based on lightness. Values below LowValue use LowColor, above HighValue use HighColor. GLQuantizeRendererFeature A post process that reduces the number of distinct color values in the image, creating a posterized or stylized effect. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#quantize. GLSimpleOutlineRendererFeature A post process that produces an outline. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#simple-outline. GLTriToneMapRendererFeature Maps the image’s tones to three colors (low, mid, and high) based on lightness, smoothly blending between them using inverse linear interpolation. See ../common/docs/effects-reference-common.html#tri-tone-map.

feature is the URP counterpart to the built-in SeparablePostProcess<TShaderProperties>. Only executes for cameras that passes the AllowedPostProcessCamera mask. A separable effect is executed in two one-dimensional passes: A horizontal pass with direction (1, 0). A vertical pass with direction (0, 1). This reduces the cost of filtering operations such as box blurs and Gaussian blurs compared to a full two-dimensional kernel. The feature creates two materials from the same shader and enqueues two render passes at the configured UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal.RenderPassEvent. Kernel parameters and other shader properties are applied automatically before each pass. On Unity 6 and newer with render graph enabled, passes use RecordRenderGraph and UnityEngine.Rendering.RenderGraphModule.Util.RenderGraphUtils.AddBlitPass. On older versions or when compatibility mode is active, the legacy Execute path is used with CommandBuffer.Blit. [Serializable] public sealed class MultiWashProperties : ShaderProperties Inheritance object ShaderProperties MultiWashProperties Inherited Members ShaderProperties.MaterialVersion ShaderProperties.IncMaterialVersion() ShaderProperties.Shader ShaderProperties.RequiresDepthTexture ShaderProperties.RequiresNormalsTexture ShaderProperties.CheckMaterialVersion() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This effect needs four materials (its own MultiWash combine shader, the internal Gamelogic.Fx.WaterColor.PostProcessing.Effects.MultiWashProperties.Layer threshold shader used once per layer, the internal Wash shader, and Blur), so hosts (MultiWashPostProcess, GLMultiWashRendererFeature) run a bespoke multi-pass pipeline per layer: threshold (GetLayerThreshold(int), black level fixed at 0) → blur (horizontal then vertical) → wash (offsetting the noise texture per layer via GetLayerNoiseOffset(int) to decorrelate layers), then combine every layer's wash result via this effect's own shader, calling SetLayerTexture(Material, int, Texture) for each layer in use. The per-layer threshold shader and its fixed black level of 0 are an internal implementation detail of the algorithm (not user-tunable, unlike the standalone Layer effect), so the threshold pass is not exposed as a serialized field here. Fields MaxLayerCount Maximum number of layers supported by the MultiWash shader (fixed number of texture slots declared in MultiWash.shader). public const int MaxLayerCount = 5 Field Value int Properties LayerCount Number of layers to blend together. public int LayerCount { get; set; } Property Value int ShaderName Gets the name of the shader used by this property set. public override string ShaderName { get; } Property Value string Remarks This name is passed to the internal shader lookup system when the properties are enabled. It should match the full shader path as defined in the shader file. Wash Blur and wash shader properties, shared across every layer. public WashProperties Wash { get; } Property Value WashProperties Methods GetLayerNoiseOffset(int) Per-layer tiling offset applied to NoiseTexture, decorrelating layers via a golden-ratio increment. public Vector2 GetLayerNoiseOffset(int layerIndex) Parameters layerIndex int Returns Vector2 GetLayerThreshold(int) The threshold used for the given zero-based layer index, evenly spaced across (0, 1). public float GetLayerThreshold(int layerIndex) Parameters layerIndex int Returns float OnEnable() Called when the owning component or asset is enabled. public override void OnEnable() Remarks The default implementation resolves the shader using ShaderName. Subclasses overriding this method should normally call base.OnEnable(). OnValidate() Called when serialized values are changed in the inspector. public override void OnValidate() Remarks Override this method to clamp values, enforce invariants, or perform lightweight validation in response to inspector edits. SetLayerMaterialProperties(Material, int) Sets the material properties for the internal per-layer threshold pass: GetLayerThreshold(int) for layerIndex, with black level fixed at 0. public void SetLayerMaterialProperties(Material layerMaterial, int layerIndex) Parameters layerMaterial Material layerIndex int SetLayerTexture(Material, int, Texture) Sets one of the _Layer0.._Layer4 texture slots on the combine material. public void SetLayerTexture(Material effectMaterial, int layerIndex, Texture layerTexture) Parameters effectMaterial Material layerIndex int layerTexture Texture SetMaterialProperties(Material) Applies all shader-related properties to the given material. public override void SetMaterialProperties(Material effectMaterial) Parameters effectMaterial Material Remarks Subclasses should override this method and set all relevant shader uniforms (for example, floats, vectors, colors, textures, and keywords). Do not call IncMaterialVersion() here. By the time this method is called the material has already been fetched, so any increment would take effect one frame late. Staleness checks belong in CheckMaterialVersion(). SetWashMaterialProperties(Material, int) Sets Wash's material properties for the given layer index, offsetting the noise texture tiling by GetLayerNoiseOffset(int) to decorrelate layers. The user-configured NoiseTextureTilingOffset is temporarily adjusted for this call and restored immediately after, so it is not permanently altered. public void SetWashMaterialProperties(Material washMaterial, int layerIndex) Parameters washMaterial Material layerIndex int Remarks Does not set the blurred source texture — call SetBlurredTexture(Material, Texture) for that, after running the internal blur pass.

api/Gamelogic.Fx.html.summary: Namespace Gamelogic.Fx Classes ApplyDepthCompensationKeyword BoolKeyword A serialized bool that drives a single shader_feature keyword when true. Subclass and override Keyword to name the keyword - the identity is code, not serialized data, so it can never drift from a renamed shader keyword. EnumKeyword<TEnum> A serialized enum that drives one shader_feature keyword from a fixed set, based on its current value. Subclass and override Keywords to name them (positional, matching the enum's underlying int values; use "_" for a value that maps to no keyword) - identity is code, not serialized data. FloatMatrix A serializable data-driven dither matrix. Stores an array of normalized float values along with matrix dimensions. HexGridKeyword Drives the HEX_GRID keyword when GridType is Hex. Shared across every effect that offers a hex/rect grid choice (Pixelate, dither bias, ...). Interval Represents an interval of floats. IntervalRangeAttribute Use this on inspector fields of type Interval to limit tha range. Keyword Represents a shader keyword, and whether it is present or not. KeywordSet Represents a set of mutually exclusive keywords of a shader. MaterialExtensions Provides extension methods for configuring materials used by Gamelogic Fx effects. These helpers simplify setting keyword collections, texture tiling, color lists, and kernel parameters in a consistent and centralized way. MatrixArray Represents a two-dimensional matrix stored internally as a flat float array. The matrix layout and interpretation are controlled by the dimensions field. RGBMatrix Three FloatMatrix instances — one per color channel — plus a shared "all-channels" matrix, with a Locked flag that determines which matrices are active. RequiresMixboxAttribute Used to flag components that need Mixbox to work. StringKeyword A serialized string that drives one shader_feature keyword picked from a popup, backed by the same PropertyDrawerData value-registry used by [StringPopup] fields. Subclass and override RetrieverKey to name the value-list registry key - identity is code, not serialized data. UseUvMapKeyword UvAdaptiveBackgroundBlendKeyword Interfaces IFloatMatrix Represents a read-only view of a two-dimensional matrix of float values. IShaderFeatureKeyword A serialized field type that drives one or more shader_feature keywords. Implementing this lets GetActiveShaderFeatureKeywords() discover the field via reflection instead of each Properties class listing it by hand. Enums GridType The cell geometry used by grid-based effects such as pixelation and dither bias. Interval.ViewType Determines how the interval is displayed in the inspector. OutlineSource Ways to select the source for outline edge detection.

common/docs/ai.html.title: | Gamelogic Fx
common/docs/ai.html.summary: AI Skills Gamelogic Fx ships AI Skills -- structured SKILL.md files that let Unity's built-in AI Assistant understand and drive this package's effects, map renderers, and tools directly from natural-language requests, instead of you having to know the exact component names and menu paths yourself. Warning 🧪 Experimental. AI Skills are a new, actively-evolving feature of both this package and of Unity's own AI Assistant. Behavior, accuracy, and the exact setup steps may change between Unity versions. Treat any AI-driven change to your project the way you would treat any other automated edit -- review it before committing. Getting it going Unity's AI Assistant discovers skills automatically once it's installed and skills are allowed to run -- there's no manual step needed to "load" this package's skills beyond having the AI Assistant enabled in your project and pointed at a conversation that can see this package. Because the exact enablement flow (menus, preference toggles, permission prompts) lives inside Unity's own evolving AI tooling rather than this package, we don't document the click-by-click steps here -- consult Unity's own AI Assistant documentation for the current setup flow, then just ask it for what you want in plain language, using the kinds of prompts below as a starting point. Example prompts These exercise the core Gamelogic Fx skills directly -- map renderers, the general-purpose post effects, and the texture-generation tools: "render a depth map for my scene and use it to drive an outline effect" "make hatching/dithering follow surface curvature using a normal map" (see the Dithering/Cross-hatching examples below for the effect-specific side of this) "add a blur, then posterize the result" "generate a Voronoi texture I can use as a pattern" "what post effects does gamelogic fx include for tone mapping?"

common/docs/changes.html.summary: Changes [6.1.0] 2026-08-30 🎉 New Features Added AI Skills, so this package's features can be used with Unity's AI Assistant. [6.0.0] 2026-08-27 🐞 Bug Fixes Fixed scenes sometimes rendering black under URP RenderGraph: removed a stray _BlitTexture_TexelSize definition in Gamelogic.hlsl. Removed an erroneous camera-scope check in RenderGraph_MapPass (URP) referencing ExperimentalSettings, a class removed in [4.0.0]. Camera-scope filtering already happens upstream via CameraScope. Fixed post-process/map shaders sometimes rendering with the wrong (default) variant, or going black, depending on the active render pipeline: Unity's shader stripping could remove the GAMELOGIC_HAS_URP/GAMELOGIC_HAS_URP_RENDER_GRAPH variant actually in use. Fixed by auto-generating a ShaderVariantCollection that records the variants actually configured in the project (covers all effect keywords, not just pipeline ones) and keeping it registered in Preloaded Shaders. See the new Shader Stripping page for details. Fixed shaders rendering grey after switching the active render pipeline asset live (no domain reload), in both the editor and builds: PipelineDefiner only ever set its shader keywords once, on load, so a later live switch left them stale. Now also re-applies on RenderPipelineManager.activeRenderPipelineAssetChanged. Fixed compilation issues due to incompatible API calls or old code on certain versions of Unity. 📄 Documentation Fixed how-to-use-map-renderers.md/how-to-use-post-effects.md: replaced the removed ExperimentalSettings overlay-camera API with the current Camera Scope setting. 💀 Breaking Changes RenderGraph is now always used when available, regardless of URP's Render Compatibility Mode setting. [5.1.0] 2026-07-18 🐞 Bug Fixes PostProcessRendererFeature<T> and GLMapRendererFeature<T> (URP) now poll CheckMaterialVersion() every frame and recreate their material(s) when the version changes, matching the Built-In PostProcess<T> host. Previously, resizing a variable-size array property (for example a dither matrix) while using the URP renderer feature left the material with the old array size. No current map effect uses this yet, but GLMapRendererFeature<T> is now wired up the same way. PostProcessRendererFeature<T>.Create(), SeparableRendererFeature<T>.Create(), and GLMapRendererFeature<T>.Create() no longer leak resources when Unity calls Create() again (which happens on every enable/disable, every Inspector edit anywhere in the feature, and after script reload — not just once). The render pass(es) are still rebuilt every time (needed since injectionPoint is baked into the pass constructor with no way to update it later), but now properly release their native resources first via the new PostEffectPass.ReleaseResources(). The material(s) are only (re)created when actually missing, instead of being unconditionally destroyed and reallocated on every unrelated property edit. MapPass/RenderGraph_MapPass no longer create or own their material/backgroundMaterial — ownership moved to GLMapRendererFeature<T>, which now applies the same "recreate only when missing" rule described above. Also fixes a latent NullReferenceException risk in GLMapRendererFeature<T>.AddRenderPasses when the pass was null (for example, if Create() had bailed out due to a missing shader) — it now falls back to Create() the same way PostProcessRendererFeature<T> does. Added PostEffectPass.ReleaseResources() to release the pass's CommandBuffer and RTHandle — neither was ever released when a pass was discarded, which happened on every Create() call regardless of the fix above. Fixed FxUtils.UpdateMaterial: when shader is null, it now destroys the existing material before dropping the reference. Previously it just set the reference to null, leaking the material if a map's shader ever went from valid to null at runtime. FxUtils.CreateMaterial's non-URP branch now sets hideFlags = HideFlags.DontSave on the material it creates, matching every other material-creation site (the URP branch already got this for free from CoreUtils.CreateEngineMaterial). Added MapRenderer<T> (Built-In) OnValidate, so map property edits refresh the material reactively instead of only on OnEnable/the manual Rebind button. Also wired CheckMaterialVersion polling into CreateOrUpdateMaterials (called every frame from BuildCommandBuffer, matching PostProcess<T>/GLMapRendererFeature<T>) — no current map effect needs it yet, but the hookup is now consistent across all four hosts. Fixed FloatMatrixGUI.DrawSizeControls: the +/− row/column buttons mutated the live FloatMatrix directly (correctly bumping SizeVersion), then called ApplyModifiedPropertiesWithoutUndo() against a SerializedObject buffer that predated the mutation — silently reverting SizeVersion back to its stale value and leaving MaterialVersion unable to detect the resize. Now calls serializedObject.Update() instead, which re-pulls the entire current object state (including SizeVersion) into the buffer. Also hardened FloatMatrixGUI.DrawChannelContents's preset-apply callback, which had no sync step at all, with the same Update() call. [5.0.0] 2026-07-15 🎉 New Features Added GridType enum (Hex / Rect) for use with grid-based effects such as Pixelate and Dither Grid Bias. Added Interval — a serializable float range with Min, Max, Center, and HalfSize properties, and an editor drawer that supports both min/max and center/half-size display modes. Added RGBMatrix — three FloatMatrix instances (one per channel) plus a shared All matrix, controlled by a Locked flag. Used by the Dither Grid Bias effect. Added GamelogicFxSettings (URP, experimental) — a static settings class for pipeline-level configuration such as AllowedPostProcessCamera. Pixelate effect and PixelateProperties now support a Hex grid type (pointy-top hexagonal cells) via the new GridType property. Pixelate now supports a Grid Angle property (±90°, inspector slider) to rotate the pixel grid, for both rect and hex modes. Rect mode now uses the same 9×9 jitter antialiasing as hex mode, with the rotation correctly applied in screen-pixel space. Pixelate pixel grid is now anchored to the screen centre rather than the corner, so the grid is symmetric around the render target regardless of pixel size or rotation angle. Added hex and rect grid conversion functions to Gamelogic.hlsl: pointy_hex_world_to_grid, pointy_hex_grid_to_world, and rect_world_to_grid. ⚙️ Editor Improvements Added FloatMatrixGUI — a reusable editor GUI helper for drawing FloatMatrix fields with resize controls. Added RGBMatrixPropertyDrawer — property drawer for RGBMatrix with per-channel tabs (All / R / G / B). Added IntervalPropertyDrawer — property drawer for Interval supporting both min/max and center/half-size display modes. Added GridTypeDrawer — property drawer for GridType that renders as inline toolbar buttons (Rect / Hex) instead of a dropdown. Added StringDropdownPopup — a reusable editor utility for string selection dropdowns. [4.0.0] 2026-05-16 🎉 New Features Added updateCameraEachFrame to MapRenderer so maps can render correctly when source camera properties change. Added SourceCamera to MapRenderer so maps can render correctly when the source camera changes to a different one. Added MapProperties to MapRenderer so map properties can be modified by script. Added setter properties on subclasses of MapRenderer to allow modifying them by script. Added CameraScope property to renderer features to give some control on which cameras to apply renderer features to. Added PixelOffset to PixelateProperties, allowing the pixel grid to be shifted in screen pixels. Added RenderDataExtensions with FindFeature<T>, FindRequiredFeature<T>, and FindFeatures<T> extension methods on ScriptableRendererData for convenient renderer feature lookup by type. Added ProceduralMaskedPostProcessRunner, a Built-In pipeline post-process runner that blends a stack of child effects using a procedurally computed mask — either a half-plane (line) or an ellipse — with configurable centre, angle, softness, invert, and radii parameters. 🐞 Bug Fixes Fixed issues where maps where not handling renderer-specific issues correctly. This caused ID maps to render in only one color and UV maps to ignore tiling. 📄 Documentation Improved documentation for map renderers. 💀 Breaking Changes Removed CreateSimplePass from PostEffectRenderFeature. Removed ExperimentalSettings. [3.0.1] 2026-04-15 🎉 New Features Startup wizard now displays context features. Added ExperimentalSettings. 🐞 Bug Fixes Post-processing and mapping renderer features now skip overlay cameras. 🔧 Engineering Updated to Extensions 4.6.1. Made compatible with Unity 6.4. [3.0.0] 2026-03-15 🎉 New Features Now URP works fully with RenderGraph! Added layer masking for map renderers. 🐞 Bug Fixes Effects stay active when changing scenes in the editor. [2.1.0] 2026-03-08 🎉 New Features Made it possible to differentiate between play and edit mode when setting map renderers to refresh their render lists each frame or once only. URP map renderers now refresh their render lists when a new scene is loaded. 🐞 Bug Fixes Fixed bugs where map renderers would throw errors when changing scenes. Fixed map renderers sometimes trying to get meshes from renderers that have been destroyed. [2.0.1] 2026-03-07 🐞 Bug Fixes Fixed a bug in ShaderProperty.SetOn where the IntegerArray case wrote into floatArrayValue assuming it was non-null and the correct size, which could cause a NullReferenceException or IndexOutOfRangeException at runtime. Fixed a bug in ShaderPropertyThrowHelper.WarnIfExceeds where the argName parameter was declared as int instead of string, causing incorrect formatting in warning messages. Fixed a bug in FxUtils.DestroyMaterial (URP branch) where the parameter was named shader and the body referenced an undeclared variable materialToUpdate instead of the material parameter. Fixed a typo in PropertyNotfoundException — renamed to PropertyNotFoundException to match .NET conventions. The old name is kept as an obsolete alias. Fixed an inconsistent class name: GLNormalMapRenderer has been renamed to GLNormalMapRendererFeature to match sibling classes. The old name is kept as obsolete. 🔧 Engineering Updated to Extensions 4.6.0. 📄 Documentation Updated documentation fixing typos and other errors, and adding missing documentation. ⬆️ Upgrade Notes PropertyNotfoundException is now PropertyNotFoundException. The old name is obsolete and will be removed in a future version. GLNormalMapRenderer is now GLNormalMapRendererFeature. The old name is obsolete and will be removed in a future version. [1.1.0] - 2025-12-10 🎉 New Features Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.BoxBlur post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.GaussianBlur post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.ConvexHullMap post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.MixboxConvexHullMap post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.MaxFilter post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.MinFilter post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.PowerMeanFilter post-process . Added @Gamelogic.Fx.BuiltIn.PostProcessing.Effects.SeparableNamedShaderPostProcess component . Added Smooth Noise and MultiChannel Smooth Noise generation options to the Pattern Texture Generator tool . Moved @Gamelogic.Fx.ShaderProperty and @Gamelogic.Fx.ShaderPropertyType to the Gamelogic.Fx.Internal namespace . Moved @Gamelogic.Fx.ShaderPropertyDrawer to the Gamelogic.Fx.Editor namespace . Added MixboxFunctions.hlsl. [1.0.0] - 2025-11-18 Initial release of Gamelogic Fx Dithering package.

common/docs/effects-reference-common.htm.summary: Effects reference: Common This image shows the original scene without any post processing. Icon Key Symbols used in the property reference tables throughout these docs. Icon Meaning 🖼️ Texture field. 🎨 Color field. 🔢 Matrix field. 🔑 Shader keyword. Selecting this property switches the effect's shader between shader_feature variants. See Shader Stripping if you plan to change one of these dynamically at runtime rather than through the Inspector. Add Texture Adds a texture (remapped to specified min amd max) to the image. 🔑 Property Range Description Overlay Texture 🖼️ The texture image to add. Min [-1, 1] The minimum value to remap the texture to. Max [-1, 1] The maximum value to remap the texture to. Tip To ignore a channel, make the two values equal for that channel. For example, Min = (-.1, -.1, -.1, 0) and Max = (.1, .1, .1, 0) will leave the alpha channel in tact. Adjust Gamma Adjust the gamma of the image. 🔑 Property Range Description Gamma (0, ∞) When 1.0, no change is made. Values less than 1.0 darken the image, while values greater than 1.0 lighten it. Adjust Saturation Adjusts the color saturation of the image by interpolating between grayscale luminance and the original color. 🔑 Property Range Description Saturation [0, 2) Controls color intensity. 1 leaves the image unchanged, 0 fully desaturates to grayscale. Values greater than 1 increase saturation. Saturation 0.2 Saturation 2.0 Bilateral Filter Separable Smooths and denoises the image while preserving edges, by combining spatial proximity with color similarity. Non-edge regions become soft and clean, while sharp features remain intact. Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Other Properties 🔑 Property Range Description Spatial Sigma (0, ∞) Controls how strongly the filter considers spatial distance. Larger values spread influence farther. Range Sigma (0, 1) Controls sensitivity to color differences. Lower values preserve edges more strongly. Tip Use a small Range Sigma to keep edges crisp while denoising flat regions. Increase Spatial Sigma for broader smoothing. This filter works best on noisy images or stylized materials where texture detail must be preserved around edges. Blend Texture Blends an overlay texture with the image based on its alpha and the specified opacity. 🔑 Property Range Description Overlay Texture 🖼️ The texture to blend with the image. The original alpha is respected. Opacity [0, 1] Controls the strength of the blend. A value of 0 shows only the original image, while 1 applies the overlay fully (modulated by the overlay’s alpha). 🔑 Use Mask true / false When enabled, a mask texture controls per-pixel blend strength. Mask Texture 🖼️ Greyscale mask used to restrict where the overlay is applied. White = full blend, black = no blend. Only used when Use Mask is enabled. Tip Use this for setting constant, full-screen textures (with opacity 1). This is useful for debugging > or tweaking post effects. This is also useful to add noise, an important ingredient in many effects. Box Blur Separable Applies a uniform blur by averaging samples. Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Convex Hull Map Maps each pixel’s color toward a set of primary colors using iterative convex‐hull projection. This effect gradually shifts colors toward the provided primaries, producing posterized, clustered, or palette–constrained looks. 🔑 Property Range Description Level Count [1, ∞) Number of refinement iterations. Higher values move colors closer to the convex hull defined by the primary colors. Background Color 🎨 Starting reference color used in the convex-hull projection process. Primary Colors (0–9) 🎨 Palette colors that define the convex hull. Pixel colors are iteratively pulled toward these anchors. Primary Color Count [1, 10] Number of primary colors currently active in the convex hull. Tip Use this to constrain an image to a defined palette without hard quantization. Increasing Level Count produces stronger convergence toward the chosen colors. Works well for stylized looks: painterly clusters, reduced palettes, or “vectorized” color fields. Desaturate Removes color saturation from the image, producing a grayscale result based on luminance. (This effect has no adjustable properties. It fully desaturates the image according to its luminance.) Gaussian Blur Separable Applies a smooth, natural-looking blur using a Gaussian weight curve. Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Other properties 🔑 Property Range Description Sigma (0, ∞) Controls how quickly the Gaussian curve falls off. Higher values produce a softer, more spread-out blur. Tip Typically, you can use Sigma = Kernel Size / 6. Invert Inverts the colors of the image. Max Filter Separable Replaces each pixel with the maximum color value found in its neighborhood. This effect behaves like a morphological dilation on color channels. Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Min Filter Separable Replaces each pixel with the minimum color value found in its neighborhood. This effect behaves like a morphological erosion on color channels. Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Mixbox Convex Hull Map Requires Mixbox. Maps each pixel’s color toward a set of primary colors using iterative convex-hull projection, but blends using Mixbox, a perceptually accurate subtractive color-mixing model. This produces smoother, more natural transitions than standard linear interpolation. If Mixbox is unavailable, the shader outputs a flat yellow fallback. 🔑 Property Range Description Mixbox LUT 🖼️ Lookup texture required for Mixbox’s perceptually accurate subtractive color blending. Level Count [1, ∞) Number of refinement iterations. Higher values move colors closer to the convex hull defined by the primary colors. Background Color 🎨 Starting reference color used for Mixbox convex-hull projection. Primary Colors (0–9) 🎨 Palette colors that define the convex hull. Pixel colors are iteratively blended toward these anchors using Mixbox. Primary Color Count [1, 10] Number of primary colors currently active in the convex hull. Tip Produces richer, more paint-like results than the standard Convex Hull Map thanks to Mixbox’s subtractive mixing. Ideal for watercolor, gouache, and ink-style looks. Increase Level Count for stronger palette attraction. Try limiting the primary set (e.g., only 3–5 colors) for highly stylized palettes. Pixelate Applies a pixelation effect to the image by sampling blocks of pixels instead of individual texels. 🔑 Property Range Description 🔑 Grid Type Hex/Rect Cell geometry used for the pixel grid. Hex snaps to pointy-top hexagonal cells; Rect snaps to square cells. Pixel Size (1, ∞)² Width and height of each pixel block in screen pixels. Higher values produce larger blocks. Pixel Offset ℝ² Shifts the pixel grid by this many screen pixels. Only used in Rect mode. Power Mean Separable Blurs the image by computing a power mean (p-norm mean) of neighboring pixels. Different Power values interpolate smoothly between familiar filters: Power = 1 → arithmetic mean, standard box blur Power = 2 → RMS-like mean (stronger emphasis on brighter values) Power → ∞ → approaches a max filter Power → -∞ → approaches a Min filter Separable Properties 🔑 Properties Range Description Kernel Size [0, ∞) The number of pixels sampled. KernelOffset (-∞, ∞) Where the kernel should start relative to the pixel. This is set by the shader internally to center kernels (even-sized kernels are 0.5 to the right of the center). Jump Size (0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling step size. Use values greater than 1 for faster, softer blurs. Direction — The blur direction (1,0) for horizontal, (0,1) for vertical. Internally set by the renderer. Tip Increasing the Jump Size can be a cheap way to fake a bigger kernel, but it does not always work. Other Properties 🔑 Property Range Description Power (-∞, ∞) Controls the type of mean. Lower values emphasize dark tones, higher values emphasize bright tones. Tip Can be used for "soft" min or max filters. Quantize Reduces the number of distinct color values in the image, creating a posterized or stylized effect. 🔑 Property Range Description Level Count [2, ∞) Specifies the number of quantization levels for each color channel (R, G, B). Higher values preserve more detail. Smoothness [0, 1] Controls the softness of transitions between quantized levels. A value of 0 produces hard edges, while higher values blend the steps smoothly. Tip With a low number of levels, many of the resulting colors turn out gray if each channel has the same number of level, leading to a dull result. By setting a different number of levels for at least one channel you get a more colorful result. This is with Smoothness = 0 (hard transitions). The level count is 2 for red, 4 for the other 2. This is with Smoothness = 0.1 (smooth transitions). Quad Tone Map A smooth 4-way threshold effect using inverse lerp (linear blend). Interpolates between Low–Mid0, Mid0–Mid1, and Mid1–High based on lightness. Values below LowValue use LowColor, above HighValue use HighColor. 🔑 Property Range Description Low Color 🎨 Color used for values below LowValue. Mid0 Color 🎨 Color used for the first mid range (between LowValue and Mid0Value). Mid1 Color 🎨 Color used for the second mid range (between Mid0Value and Mid1Value). High Color 🎨 Color used for values above Mid1Value. Low Value [0, 1] Lower threshold for lightness. Mid0 Value [0, 1] Threshold separating low and mid0 regions. Mid1 Value [0, 1] Threshold separating mid0 and mid1 regions. High Value [0, 1] Upper threshold for lightness. Simple Outline Detects edges in the image using a Sobel-style filter and draws an outline based on a configurable threshold. Edges can be detected from the original image, scene depth, scene normals, or an explicit source texture. 🔑 Property Range Description 🔑 Outline Source {0, 1, 2, 3} Selects the source used for edge detection. See Outline Sources below. Jump Size [0, ∞) Multiplies the sampling offset. Larger values produce thicker, coarser outlines. Edge Factor [0, ∞) Scales the detected edge strength before thresholding. Used to make threshold tuning easier. Threshold [0, ∞) Edge strength above which a pixel is considered part of an outline. Line Color 🎨 Color used to draw detected edges. Alpha controls how much it blends over the original image. Background Color 🎨 Color used where no edge is detected. Alpha controls blending with the original image. Outline Sources Camera Color – Uses the rendered image. Alternate Texture – Uses an explicitly provided texture (outlineSourceTexture) as the edge source. Depth Texture – Detects edges from scene depth. Normals Texture – Detects edges from scene normals. Using Depth and Normals Textures This effect can derive edges from scene depth or scene normals, but the setup differs depending on the render pipeline. Built-in Render Pipeline When using Depth Texture or Normals Texture as the outline source, you must ensure the camera generates the required textures. Options: Set the camera’s depthTextureMode manually: Depth for depth-based outlines DepthNormals for normal-based outlines Or add the RequiresDepthNormals component to the camera, which configures this automatically. If the required textures are not enabled, depth- or normal-based outline modes will not work. Universal Render Pipeline (URP) Nothing is required to enable depth or normals textures in URP, as this is handled internally. However, sometimes the normals don't work in the editor. Playing the game usually fixes this. Tip To draw outlines over the original image, set Background Color alpha to 0 and Line Color alpha to 1. If the outline is hard to tune, start with Edge Factor = 1, find usable lower and upper threshold bounds, then adjust Edge Factor to bring the threshold into a convenient range. You can render out an IDMap and use it as the AlternateTexture source to outline objects. The Jump distance is a cheap way to control outline thickness, but may produce artifacts on thin features. A better approach is to use a Min filter (for dark outlines) or Max filter (for light outlines) after the outline pass. Tri-tone Map Maps the image’s tones to three colors (low, mid, and high) based on lightness, smoothly blending between them using inverse linear interpolation. 🔑 Property Range Description Low Color 🎨 The color applied to the darkest areas of the image. Mid Color 🎨 The color applied to mid-range tones. High Color 🎨 The color applied to the brightest areas of the image. Low Value [0, 1] The threshold below which pixels are tinted entirely with the Low Color. Mid Value [0, 1] The midpoint that controls the blend between low and high regions. High Value [0, 1] The threshold above which pixels are tinted entirely with the High Color. Tip Use this effect for quick-and-dirty color grading. This is an easy way to make monochromatic effects more lively.
